title: Exact orders under isotropic cylinder substitution and controlled division
statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $R=F[[u_1,\ldots,u_n]]$ and $S=F[[u_1,\ldots,u_n,t]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $K\subseteq R$ be a finitely generated ideal and $d\ge1$, and assume $K\subseteq(u_1,\ldots,u_n)^d$. Define the order of an ideal to be the supremum of the powers of the displayed maximal ideal containing it, with order $\infty$ for zero. If $K\ne0$, write $m=\operatorname{ord}_{(u)}K$, which is finite and at least $d$. For each integer $k\ge1$ let $K_k\subseteq S$ be the ideal generated by $t^{-kd}f(t^ku_1,\ldots,t^ku_n)$, for $f$ in any finite generating set of $K$. These are power series, the ideal does not depend on the chosen generators, and
$$\sup\{q:K_k\subseteq(t)^q\}=k(m-d),\qquad\operatorname{ord}_{(u,t)}K_k=(k+1)m-kd.$$
More generally, if $i\ge0$ and $id\le k(m-d)$, the ideal $K_{k,i}=t^{-id}K_k$ is a power-series ideal and satisfies
$$\sup\{q:K_{k,i}\subseteq(t)^q\}=k(m-d)-id,\quad\operatorname{ord}_{(u,t)}K_{k,i}=(k+1)m-(k+i)d,$$
$$K_{k,i}\subseteq(t)^d\ \Longleftrightarrow\ k(m-d)\ge(i+1)d.$$
For $K=0$, all these ideals are zero for every $k\ge1$ and $i\ge0$; their two orders are $\infty$ and all the displayed containment tests hold. In particular the zero case also covers $n=0$.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak m=(u_1,\ldots,u_n)$ and $\mathfrak n=(u_1,\ldots,u_n,t)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with coefficient ring $F$ and coefficient ideal $J=0$, first in $n$ and then in $n+1$ variables. Since $0^r=0$ for $r>0$, membership in $\mathfrak m^q$ or $\mathfrak n^q$ is exactly vanishing of all coefficients of total degree below $q$. Thus for a finite generating family $(f_j)$ of a nonzero ideal $K$, the least degree $m$ of a nonzero coefficient among all $f_j$ is finite and equals $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak m}K$: all generators lie in $\mathfrak m^m$, whereas a generator attaining that degree does not lie in $\mathfrak m^{m+1}$. Containment of a generated ideal in any ideal is equivalent to containment of each generator, by closure under finite sums and multiplication. The assumption gives $m\ge d$. The same criterion computes the total order of every finitely generated ideal in $S$ from its generators.

proof.text:
For $\alpha\in\mathbf N^n$ write $|\alpha|=\sum_l\alpha_l$ and $u^\alpha=\prod_lu_l^{\alpha_l}$. Using the coefficient-family and finite Cauchy-product definition [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], define
$$\phi_k(\sum_\alpha c_\alpha u^\alpha)=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha u^\alpha t^{k|\alpha|}.$$
For each coefficient $(\alpha,b)$ this assigns $c_\alpha$ if $b=k|\alpha|$, and zero otherwise, so the series is defined without any convergence assumption. It preserves constants and addition. In a product, a pair of source exponents $\alpha,\beta$ contributes at $(\alpha+\beta,k|\alpha|+k|\beta|)$; since $|\alpha+\beta|=|\alpha|+|\beta|$, the finite convolution is exactly the coefficient of $\phi_k(fg)$. Hence $\phi_k$ is an $F$-algebra homomorphism, sending $u_l$ to $t^ku_l$. In particular this coefficient formula is the indicated formal substitution. Distinct source exponents retain distinct $u$-exponents, so no two source coefficients merge.

proof.text:
A series $H=\sum_{\alpha,b}h_{\alpha,b}u^\alpha t^b$ belongs to $(t)^a$ exactly when $h_{\alpha,b}=0$ for $b<a$: multiplication by $t^a$ shifts the $t$-index by $a$, and the converse quotient has coefficient $h_{\alpha,b+a}$. This also proves uniqueness of the quotient and injectivity of multiplication by $t^a$. For $f=\sum c_\alpha u^\alpha\in K$, step 1 gives $c_\alpha=0$ if $|\alpha|<d$, so define
$$T_k(f)=\sum_{|\alpha|\ge d}c_\alpha u^\alpha t^{k(|\alpha|-d)}.$$
Its exponents are nonnegative and $t^{kd}T_k(f)=\phi_k(f)$. This operation is additive on $K$, and for $a\in R$, multiplication by $t^{kd}$ shows $T_k(af)=\phi_k(a)T_k(f)$, by step 2 and the just-proved injectivity. If $f=\sum_ja_jf_j$, it follows that $T_k(f)=\sum_j\phi_k(a_j)T_k(f_j)$. Therefore the ideal generated by $T_k(f_j)$ equals the ideal generated by all $T_k(f)$ with $f\in K$, and is independent of the chosen finite generators. It is precisely $K_k$.

proof.text:
Assume $K
e0$. Every nonzero coefficient $c_\alpha$ of a generator has $|\alpha|\ge m$, and in its $T_k$-image it occurs unchanged at $(\alpha,k(|\alpha|-d))$. The $t$-exponent is at least $A=k(m-d)$ and the total degree is at least $B=(k+1)m-kd$. A generator and exponent attaining $|\alpha|=m$ in step 1 attain both bounds, with the same nonzero coefficient; distinct $\alpha$ cannot cancel by step 2. The coefficient criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with $J=0$ in $n+1$ variables gives $K_k\subseteq\mathfrak n^B$ and $K_k
ot\subseteq\mathfrak n^{B+1}$. The $t$-shift criterion in step 3 likewise gives $K_k\subseteq(t)^A$ and $K_k
ot\subseteq(t)^{A+1}$. Each containment is checked on generators. These upper failures and lower containments prove the two claimed suprema and nonzeroness.

proof.text: Let $a=id\le A$. All generators of $K_k$ have $t$-exponents at least $a$, so divide each by $t^a$ using step 3. The ideal generated by these quotients is exactly $t^{-a}K_k$: if $t^aH=\sum_js_jT_k(f_j)$, cancellation of $t^a$ gives $H=\sum_js_j(t^{-a}T_k(f_j))$, and multiplication gives the reverse inclusion. The quotient generator has coefficient $c_\alpha$ at $(\alpha,k(|\alpha|-d)-a)$. All these indices are nonnegative; their least $t$-exponent is $A-a$, and their least total degree is $B-a$, attained by the same degree-$m$ coefficient. The $t$-shift criterion and [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with $J=0$ therefore give orders $k(m-d)-id$ and $(k+1)m-(k+i)d$. Finally containment in $(t)^d$ holds exactly when $A-id\ge d$, equivalently $k(m-d)\ge(i+1)d$. Equality at the boundary is allowed.

proof.text: If $K=0$, every entry in any generating family is zero, so substitution and every quotient by a power of $t$ are zero by the coefficient shifts of steps 2--3. Their ideals are zero, lie in every displayed ideal power and have both suprema $\infty$. In the zero case every containment test is true; no finite $m$ is introduced and no subtraction $\infty-\infty$ is needed. If $n=0$, [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] identifies $R$ with $F$, and the empty variables ideal is zero. Since $d\ge1$, the assumption $K\subseteq0^d$ forces $K=0$, so this case is already covered.
